cohort: The study participants consisted of 88 Tunisian women with preeclampsia and 60 age- and BMI-matched normotensive control women.
finding: Increased sFLT-1 levels and the sFLT-1/PlGF ratio, but not circulating PlGF levels, are independent risk factors for preeclampsia and are significantly correlated with dysmenorrhea, hypertension, baby weight, and C-section.
mod_finding: Increased sFLT-1 levels and the sFLT-1/PlGF ratio were significantly correlated with C-section.
cross-section timing: At the time of preeclampsia diagnosis or during the preeclamptic episode for cases, and presumably during a similar gestational period for normotensive controls.
birth_weight: Baby weight was measured and found to be correlated with sFLT-1 levels and sFLT-1/PlGF ratio.
